title: How do we finish a parallelogram from two sides and an angle?
description: A line four centimetres long and a thirty degree angle give two sides, and a parallel drawn through each far end meets at the fourth corner. Keeko doubts that a shape with these sides must be a rectangle.
teaching_notes: One idea: a parallelogram has both pairs of opposite sides parallel, so two parallels fix the fourth corner. Watch for students who draw right angles at every corner because they picture a rectangle.

source: Construct a parallelogram ABCD with AB = 4 cm, AD = 5 cm and
video_script.why: The child sees that the meaning of a parallelogram is also its recipe: two parallels through the known ends meet at the last corner.
video_script.substitution: the book's own numbers: AB = 4 cm, AD = 5 cm and a 30 degree angle between them
video_script.anchor: the parallelogram ABCD drawn from the book's two sides and the 30 degree angle
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks a shape with parallel opposite sides must be a rectangle, but the angle at A is 30 degrees, not 90.
video_script.payoff_line: Eigh B C D is the required parallelogram

final_answer.value: ABCD is a parallelogram, not a rectangle
final_answer.spoken: a parallelogram that is not a rectangle

maths_rules: AB = 4 cm and AD = 5 cm, with angle DAB = 30 degrees
the line through D parallel to AB and the line through B parallel to AD meet at C
AB || DC and AD || BC, so ABCD is a parallelogram
angle A = 30 degrees, not 90 degrees, so ABCD is not a rectangle
video_script.design: One idea: two parallels fix the fourth corner. One figure, built a step at a time, stays on the board through the idea part.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks it must be a rectangle, because the opposite sides are parallel.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But a rectangle needs a right angle at every corner.
<bookmark mark='lean'/>Here the angle at eigh is only thirty degrees, so the shape leans.
<bookmark mark='kind'/>Parallel opposite sides make a parallelogram, and a rectangle is the special one with ninety degrees.
